target_customer: US Department of War and military units needing low-cost counter-drone defense
problem: Cheap first-person-view suicide drones threaten vehicles and bases, and existing defenses are expensive or not portable.
business_model: Hardware sales and contracts to the US military; claims 1.6M in sales and multiple delivered systems

founders.name: Russell Smith
previous_startups: A consultancy that helped launch Africa's largest e-commerce platform (outcome not stated)

competitors.name: Anduril
competitors.what: Counter-drone systems among broader defense products

competitors.name: Shotling
competitors.what: Short-range rotary gun system aimed at FPV drones

technical_complexity.rationale: A fast-tracking turret with computer vision, real-time targeting and a hard-kill mechanism needs robotics, perception and safety certification, and a 19 person team has already shipped it.

defensibility.rationale: Delivered systems and Army testing create a track record and procurement position, but many well-funded rivals compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. Larger defense startups were already building comparable systems when the company joined YC in 2026.

market_need_then: The war in Ukraine showed the threat of FPV and one-way attack drones, and counter-UAS startups raised over 1.2B across 15 rounds from Q1 2025 to Q1 2026 per one roundup.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Bracketed uppercase labels on the site such as COMPANY and 9 MOTHERS
identity.voice_and_tone: Terse defense-tech, ships fast, works in person

branding.brand_signature: Norse-style product names Edda, Vor, Atla and Gleipnir; no source ties them to the company name
branding.community_and_virality: Press on the product: Shephard Media on the Army live-fire test, a press release for the Spotter Global radar integration dated 2026-08-24, and a Startup Spotlight.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name and product names with early defense press, but no evidence the brand itself drives sales.

outcome_analysis: The company claims 1.6M in sales to the Department of War, delivered systems, Army testing in August 2026 and a radar integration partnership, which shows early product market fit in a drone-driven demand surge. Founders previously built and ran a YC software company. Funding amounts are unverified, so the capital story is unknown.
notes: Funding conflicts and is unverified: aggregators show 500K pre-seed (June 2026), 130K total, a 1.79M accelerator post-money, a 175M figure and a claim of a 200M plus valuation attributed to TechCrunch that was not found. No round is recorded. The 1.6M sales figure is the company claim. Competitor dates are 2025 and 2026 roundup entries, listed as of the batch.
